page: Microsoft Azure FX24-12mds_v2 is a compute- and memory-intensive virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance runs on a dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 6 physical cores supporting hyper-threading to deliver 12 vCPUs. The processor cache configuration comprises 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and an extensive 260 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 variants and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8).

A defining hardware characteristic of the instance is its memory density, providing 504.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 42.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture features a bundled 1417 GB local NVMe SSD, with support for premium storage. There are no discrete GPUs allocated to this configuration, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded throughput driven by the 4.2 GHz clock frequency. The system achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2356.0 and top-tier text processing performance of 3012.0, alongside single-threaded gzip compression at 34.85 GB/sec. Small-model language inference achieved 367.67 tokens/sec in generation. In multi-threaded workloads, the instance delivered average-tier throughput relative to its 12 vCPUs, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 11836.0, stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 13327.11, and Redis SET throughput of 18.95 million operations per second. Text generation performance degraded significantly on larger models without accelerator hardware.

The hardware configuration trades high overall core counts for high memory density per core, large L3 cache capacity, and rapid single-core frequencies. This makes the FX24-12mds_v2 efficient for applications bound by per-core software licensing costs or memory constraints. Primary workload fits include in-memory databases, memory-constrained data transformation pipelines, caching layers, and high-frequency computational tasks requiring dedicated local NVMe scratch storage.

Single-threaded performance benchmarks place the system in the upper tiers, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2356.0 and robust gzip compression speeds.
